definition: Charging $10,000 for a logo redesign because it transforms a brand's sales, regardless of how many hours it took.
A master designer finishes a complex website in 2 hours and makes $100, while a novice takes 20 hours and makes $1,000.
hint: Being faster actually earns you less money under this model.

definition: Pointing out to a client that their broken checkout page loses them $50,000 every single month they wait to fix it.
hint: What it costs the client to do nothing.

definition: Mentioning a comprehensive $50,000 corporate rebranding package first so that a $15,000 website proposal looks reasonable by comparison.
hint: Setting a high reference point for pricing.

definition: A client casually asking to 'just add a blog and a mobile app' halfway through a project without increasing the budget.
hint: When project requirements slowly grow without extra pay.

definition: A prospective client treating high-level marketing strategy the same as hiring cheap, interchangeable data-entry clerks on an hourly board.
hint: Treating professional services like a generic commodity.

definition: Adding an extra $5,000 buffer to a fixed-fee contract because the client's legacy software might break during integration.
hint: Extra margin for taking on project execution risk.

definition: Charging a client $2,500 for a 2-week discovery audit to map out their technical debt before bidding on the actual rebuild.
hint: Paid discovery before starting the main work.

definition: Giving a client three choices: Option A ($10k basic fix), Option B ($25k full overhaul), and Option C ($40k full overhaul plus automation).
hint: Offering multiple package choices instead of a single price.

definition: Billing based on how many hours you sat at your desk (Input) versus the 30% increase in revenue your strategy generated for the client (Outcome).
"My minimum engagement starts at $5,000—does that fit your budget expectations before we dive further?"
Asking "Are you the sole decision-maker on this project, or will a board of 6 people need to approve every change?"
Politely ending a sales call when a client wants 6 stakeholders involved for a tiny $1,000 project.
hint: Knowing when a deal is a bad fit.

definition: Stating your price range within the first 5 minutes of a call to avoid spending 2 hours pitching to someone who can't afford you.
"If this new branding helps you close two more high-ticket clients this quarter, it pays for itself tenfold."
hint: Tying your price to their return on investment.
